exposure: Hour of life at auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing
cohort: 31,984 infants tested during a standard birth hospitalization from 2014 to 2016 at Prentice Women's Hospital of Chicago.
finding: Delaying hearing screening until 10-11 hours for vaginally born infants and 30-32 hours for cesarean-born infants results in a statistically significant improvement in ABR pass rates.
mod_finding: ABR pass rates were significantly lower for cesarean-born infants compared to vaginally born infants, but delaying hearing screening improved pass rates in both groups.
